messages:
opsbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT (P1) — Elevated 5xx/timeout rate observed at gateway from 11:02:16 UTC. Pager sent to oncall. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Estimated error increase: +420% RPM.

marie.k: picking this up. oncall, do we have an initial impact summary? any customer complaints yet?

oncall: seeing a clear spike starting 11:02:16. 502/504s and some 503s. Errors peaked ~11:05 and sustained for ~6m. No large-scale account deletions reported, but several PLG customers reported 5xx spikes via support.

raj: can someone dump sample proxy logs with correlation ids? need to trace upstream latency and retry behavior.

oncall: sharing sample entries (scrubbed) below — these are from gw-router logs around 11:04:xx. correlation_id is the request-id we use for tracing.

oncall: ```
2026-02-12T11:04:03.123Z gw-router INFO request_id=cid-8a3f upstream=ingress-a-1 response_code=502 upstream_latency_ms=2500 retries=2 route=/v1/generate
2026-02-12T11:04:04.442Z gw-router INFO request_id=cid-8a5b upstream=ingress-a-2 response_code=504 upstream_latency_ms=3000 retries=3 route=/v1/chat
2026-02-12T11:04:04.789Z gw-router INFO request_id=cid-8a7c upstream=ingress-b-1 response_code=503 upstream_latency_ms=1200 retries=1 route=/v1/generate
```

lin: interesting — retries >0 for many of these. looks like upstream is slow and we're retrying which may amplify load. any egress throttles or rate-limits fired?

sre-lead: checking egress metrics now. initial look: ingress-a shows increased latency and 5xx rate at the same timeframe. upstream p95 latency jumped from 300ms -> 2.4s. no explicit 429s, but backend instances behind ingress-a are returning 5xx.

raj: hypothesis list (to track):
- H1: upstream ingress-a service degraded (OOM, GC, slow DB) causing increased latency -> gw retries -> amplified 5xx.
- H2: a config rollout changed timeout/retry behavior causing more aggressive retries.
- H3: network flap causing transient connection resets visible as 502/504.

marie.k: prioritize H1 and H2 for mitigation. mitigation options: 1) disable gateway retries temporarily for affected routes, 2) increase gateway timeout to avoid cascading retries, 3) route traffic away from ingress-a (circuit-break).

oncall: starting quick mitigations: disabling retries for /v1/generate and /v1/chat (canary to 10% then immediate 100% if green). applying now.

deploy-bot: Config change request accepted: id=config-20260212-011. Applying to gw-router canaries (10%)...

deploy-bot: Done — gw-router canary pool: config-20260212-011 active at 10% (11:07:12 UTC).

oncall: monitoring error rate and latency. initial drop in retries seen for canary traffic.

sre-lead: after disabling retries on canary, canary error rate dropped ~35% vs baseline. good signal. rolling to 100%.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: config-20260212-011 applied to all gateways (11:09:00 UTC).

oncall: error rate across endpoints dropping but still elevated. looks like some upstream instances remain unhealthy. opening a ticket with ingress-a owners and attaching sample correlation ids.

lin: ingress-a SRE pinged — they report a control-plane job that started a mass pod restart ~10:58 which created transient load on a subset of instances. they're scaling additional replicas now.

cust-success: we got ~12 inbound tickets in the past 10m, mostly noisy errors in app logs. have informed top 3 impacted customers and provided temporary workaround (retry client-side with jitter or switch to fallback model).

marie.k: customer impact summary for post-incident notes: ~0.6% of total requests during the spike got 5xx. peak affected customers: 8 (not all paying). no major SLA breach expected but track precise counts.

raj: collect full request logs for the window 11:00-11:12. can someone run the query and upload to shared drive? include correlation ids: cid-8a3f, cid-8a5b, cid-8a7c, cid-8b01, cid-8b1f.

oncall: running query now. will paste the log archive link when ready.

oncall: Log bundle uploaded: https://internal-files.redwood/incident/2523456789/logs.tar.gz (contains gw-router logs, ingress-a metrics, and sampled traces).

sre-lead: quick trace snippet (from distributed-tracing) showing retry loop:

sre-lead: ```
trace cid-8a5b: gw-router -> ingress-a -> model-worker-3
span ingress-a processing: start=11:04:02.900 end=11:04:04.425 (1525ms)
span model-worker-3: start=11:04:02.905 end=11:04:04.400 (1495ms)
status=500 at model-worker-3 -> gw-router observes timeout -> retries -> second attempt -> same outcome
```

lin: that confirms worker slowness and repeated attempts. mitigation of retries helped but root cause is worker latency. ingress-a team will isolate failing workers and restart.

marie.k: action items (in-thread track):
- A1: ingress-a SRE to provide root cause and remediation steps (assigned: Lin)
- A2: Full log + trace analysis and correlation id expansion (assigned: Raj)
- A3: Customer impact ticket consolidation and comms (assigned: Cust-Success)
- A4: Postmortem doc with timeline and prevention (assigned: Marie)

lin: ingress-a team reports they found an allocation bug in model-worker causing memory churn and long GC pauses — triggered by a recent internal config (pool_size=0). they revert config and are rolling a fix.

oncall: fix rolled: ingress-a fix v2.0.3 deployed at 11:18:40. monitoring shows backend p95 latency returning to normal over next 8 minutes.

deploy-bot: Deployment ingress-a v2.0.3 succeeded (11:18:40 UTC).

marie.k: customer comms draft — sending to #customer-comm for review: "We investigated elevated 5xxs caused by a backend configuration regression in an upstream service. We applied a fix and disabled aggressive gateway retries to limit impact. We're following with a full RCA."

cust-success: sent to impacted customers + support tickets updated.

sre-lead: preliminary RCA summary inside thread: cause = allocation bug in model-worker (config regression); amplifying factor = gateway retries + mass restarts during control-plane job; mitigation = disable retries, rollback config, deploy fix; follow-up = add safety guard for pool_size config + tighter pre-deploy checks.

marie.k: handing off overnight monitoring to Lin. Lin, please watch the traces and confirm error rate stays within normal thresholds.

lin: taking handoff. will check at 11:45 and midnight. leaving notes in the incident doc.

oncall: closing pager for now — root mitigation applied and monitoring stable for >15m. will keep thread open for RCA artifacts. :white_check_mark:

marie.k: thanks everyone. please drop any additional logs or notes into this thread. we'll schedule a follow-up postmortem meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC.

sre-lead: added timeline + hypothesis table to incident doc. final ask: Raj, paste the expanded correlation-id list you used for bulk trace lookup.

raj: expanded list uploaded to logs.tar.gz/trace-ids.txt. entries include ~430 IDs in the window 11:00-11:12.

opsbot: Incident P1 resolved by marie.k, severity downgraded to P2 at 11:28:10 UTC.

lin: noted. handing off complete.
